materials.title: Mia's Tuesday — a diary entry
contentText:
Mia's Tuesday

I woke up at seven o'clock on Tuesday morning.
I had breakfast with my family. We ate toast and drank orange juice.

Then I caught the bus to school. I arrived at half past eight.
At school, I had lunch with my friends. We ate sandwiches.

After school, I came home and did my homework.
In the evening, my family had dinner together. We ate pasta.
Later, I went to bed at nine o'clock.

materials.title: Simple Past — talking about finished actions
contentText:
Use Simple Past for finished actions in the past — things that happened and are done.

Regular verbs: add -ed to base form. walk → walked, arrive → arrived, watch → watched.

Irregular verbs change completely. Learn these six: go → went, have → had, do → did, eat → ate, see → saw, be → was (I/he/she/it) or were (we/you/they).

Important for German speakers: German says "Ich habe gegessen" (two words) for past stories. English says "I ate" — one word, no "have". This is the biggest difference.

Word order: after time words like "yesterday" or "then", subject still comes before verb. "Yesterday I went to school." Not "Yesterday went I to school."
She ate breakfast at seven o'clock.
Last week, we went to the cinema.
I ate. (English Simple Past — one word, no have)

materials.title: Put the sentences in order — Simple Past
Spot the mistake — Simple Past
contentText: Yesterday I have eaten breakfast at seven o'clock.
Yesterday I ate breakfast at seven o'clock.
Then went she to school by bus.
Then she went to school by bus.
Last week we have gone to the cinema.
Last week we went to the cinema.
She catched the bus at eight o'clock.
She caught the bus at eight o'clock.
